questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian** Satriya dancer Dr. Indira P. P. Bora** is from **Assam**. 
 
• She received 13 years of **training **in **Bharatnatyam** from **Guru Rukmini Devi Arundale** and **Kuchipudi **from **Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam**.
 
• Bora has **performed **and promoted **Satriya **in **Vietnam**, the **United States**, and **New Zealand**.
 
• She was awarded various awards including the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996** and **Padma Shri in 2020**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sattriya Dance has its origin in the ‘Sattras’ established by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th and 16th centuries. 

 
 
• The **Sattras **were established for the **propagation of Vaishnavism **and later became the religious, cultural and social hub of **Assam**.
 
• The Sattriya dance can be classified into two styles, namely ‘Paurashik Bhangi’ i.e. Tandava or Masculine style and ‘Stri Bhangi’ i.e. Lashya or feminine style.
 
• On November 15 in the year 2000, the Sangeet Natak Akademi of India recognized Sattriya as one of the eight classical dances of India.
 
 
 
• ​**Sangeet Natak Akademi**:
 
 
• It is the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country and was set up in 1953 for the preservation and promotion of the vast intangible heritage of India’s diverse culture expressed in forms of music, dance and drama.
 
• The Chairman of the Akademi is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi is an autonomous body of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• The registered office of the Akademi is at Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi.
 
 
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards** are the **highest national recognition conferred on practicing artists**.
 
 
• It is India's National Academy of **Music**, **Dance **& **Drama**, also called the Akademi Puraskar.
 
• It is the greatest honor bestowed upon those involved in the performing arts in India.
 
• **1952 **marked its **initial award**.

questions.question: Meenakshisundaram Pillai, a dance guru from the village of Pandanallur, was famous for which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meenakshisundaram Pillai **was widely recognised for **Bharatnatyam, **which is a classical dance form originating from** Tamil Nadu, India.**
 
• He was a** descendant of the Thanjavur Quartet, **a group of four brothers who were court composers in the early 19th century. 
 
• He trained many famous Bharatanatyam dancers,** including Devadasis like Pandanallur Jayalakshmi and Thangachi Ammal. **
 
• He also trained other dancers, including **Mrinalini Sarabhai, Rukmini Devi, and Tara Chaudhri. **
 
• Pillai's son-in-law, Chokkalingam Pillai, became the doyen Guru of the Pandanallur style after him
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is known for its **intricate footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions** and body movements that narrate a story or convey a message.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam****​**

 
 
• Mohiniyattam is one of the two classical dance forms that originated in Kerala, the other one being Kathakali.
 
• Mohiniyattam gets its name from the word ‘Mohini’, the feminine form of Lord Vishnu, the word means ‘dance of Mohini’.
 
• Dr. Sunanda Nair became the first in India to acquire a Master’s degree in Mohiniyattam. She completed her Ph.D. thesis in Intrinsic Lyrical Feminism in Mohiniyattam from Mumbai University.
 
• Mohiniyattam is based on Natya Shastra’s lasya style. 
 
• It has delicate movements and more feminine facial expressions.
 
• The movements are gentle and glide-like. They do not have terse rhythmic steps. 
 
• More emphasis is on the facial expressions and hand gestures
 
 
 
• **Odissi **
 
 
• Odissi, **a renowned classical dance form of India**, hails from the beautiful state of Odisha.
 
• Known for its sensuousness and lyrical beauty, this dance form, often depicted as a dance of love, seamlessly blends the human and divine aspects of life.
 
• It beautifully captures the subtle nuances of life, as well as the everyday mundane.
 
• The **origins of Odissi can be traced back to an early dance style known as Odhra Magadha.**
 
• This style is referred to as the southeastern style of classical dance in the Natya Shastra, which describes various dance forms.

questions.question: Which of the following is the unique dance tradition of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct option is__ Nati.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Nati dance is the most famous folk dance in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• A group of people performs it with accompanying musicians.
 
• Thora is the famous tribal dance of Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bihu
 
 
• Bihu is a folk dance from the northeastern Indian state of Assam, celebrated during the Bihu festival,
 
 
• which marks the Assamese New Year and the onset of the harvest season.
 
• This energetic dance is characterized by lively movements, fast-paced rhythms, and traditional instruments like the dhol (drum) and Pepa (bamboo flute), symbolizing joy and gratitude for a bountiful harvest.
 
• Both men and women participate in Bihu, dressed in traditional attire, showcasing the vibrant culture and unity of the Assamese people.
 
 
 
 
 
• Cheraw
 
 
• Cheraw, also known as the Bamboo Dance, is a traditional dance of the Mizo people in the state of Mizoram.
 
• This dance is famous for its unique use of bamboo sticks, which are rhythmically clapped together on the ground as dancers step in and out of the gaps with grace and precision.
 
• The dance requires tremendous skill, coordination, and timing and is typically performed during festive occasions and important ceremonies, embodying the cultural richness and festive spirit of Mizoram.
 
 
 
• Dandari
 
 
• Dandari is a traditional folk dance from the tribal communities of Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh, performed during the Dussehra festival.
 
• This dance involves storytelling through music and movement, with dancers forming circles and using sticks (dandas) to create rhythmic beats.
 
• Dandari dancers represent mythological characters and narrate folk tales, symbolizing the connection between the communities and their cultural heritage, as well as celebrating communal harmony and the victory of good over evil.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbelia**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia** dance is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010.
 
• Kalbelia dance is associated with the Kalbelia tribe of Rajasthan, India, and is known for its graceful movements and traditional music.
 
• It is often referred to as the "snake charmer dance" due to its fluid and sinuous movements that resemble those of a serpent.
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women, with women wearing traditional black swirling skirts adorned with silver jewelry and embroidery.
 
• Musical accompaniment typically includes instruments like the 'pungi' (a woodwind instrument), 'dholak' (a two-headed hand drum), and 'khanjari' (a tambourine-like instrument).
 
• Kalbelia dance is an integral part of the cultural heritage of Rajasthan and reflects the nomadic lifestyle of the Kalbelia community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage aims to ensure the better protection of important cultural practices and expressions around the world.
 
• India has several other elements inscribed on the list, including Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and the tradition of Vedic chanting.
